004B.name: Layer 2 tile range right edge
desc: One of the 16-bit tile-range bounds used while building the level layers. At level load it is set equal to $0049
(the first edge), and the Map16 pointer setup writes the right edge of the layer 2 tile range into it.
$0055 selects which of the $0045-$004B words the layer scroll tile loader uses.

004D.name: Last loaded column, layer 1
004D.kind: word table (index X: 0 or 2 from the scroll direction)
desc: Remembers the last 16-pixel column or row that was streamed into the layer 1 tilemap, so the scroll tile loader
only draws when the camera moves into a new one ([$4D,X] is compared with the current position).
Level load and the overworld setup set it to $FFFF, which probably means nothing has been drawn yet.
Values: $FFFF = no column cached.

004F.name: Last loaded column, layer 1 (second)
desc: Second word of the cached-column markers that start at $004D. Only ever written: level load and the
overworld setup store $FFFF here along with $004D-$0050, probably as 'nothing drawn yet'.
Values: $FFFF = reset.

0051.name: Last loaded column, layer 2
0051.kind: word table (index X: 0 or 2 from the scroll direction)
desc: Layer 2 counterpart of $004D. The scroll tile loader compares the current 16-pixel column against [$51,X] and
skips drawing if it is the same as last time. Level load resets $004D-$0054 to $FFFF.
Values: $FFFF = nothing drawn yet.

0055.name: Screen scroll direction (layer 1)
desc: Direction the screen is scrolling, used as a word-table index. The 'Scroll screen to follow Mario' routine
sets it (together with $0056) from where Mario is in the static camera region.
The layer scroll tile loader, the layer 2 stripe builders, sprite spawn on scroll and scroll sprites read it.
Level load and the overworld setup set it to 2 (so the $0047/$004B positions are used).
Values: 0 = left/up side, 2 = right/down side.

0056.name: Screen scroll direction (layer 2)
desc: Layer 2 copy of the scroll direction $0055. The scroll-follow routine writes it with the same value as $0055;
scroll sprite 0B (layer 2 on/off switch) sets it to 2 and the layer 3 handler clears it.
Read by the layer scroll tile loader and layer 2 stripe builders.
Values: 0 or 2.

0057.name: Object position in Map16 buffer
desc: Position of the level object being drawn, as an index into the current screen of the Map16 buffer
(low nibble = column, high nibble = row). 'Load one level object' derives it from the object's Y and X bytes;
every object draw routine then loads it into Y and writes tiles through the $006B pointer.
Mostly read: this is the start index each routine advances from while drawing slopes, ledges and pipes.

0059.name: Object size/extension byte
desc: Third byte of the level object being loaded. The loader copies it here and the object draw routines read it
as the width, length or variant setting (e.g. how many tiles a ledge, slope or pipe spans).
Written only while a level object is loaded; read by most of the bank $0D object routines.

005A.name: Level object number
desc: Number of the level object being processed, built by the loader from the object's bytes
([$0B] >> 4 with bits of [$0A]). The tileset object dispatchers use it as the jump table index X.
Screen exit and jump objects reuse it to hold the destination screen.

005B.name: Level orientation flags
desc: Set from the level header (via VerticalTable) at load time. Tells scrolling, collision and sprite code
whether each layer is a horizontal or a vertical level; tested all over (collision, sprites, scrolling).
Bits: Bit 0: layer 1 is vertical. Bit 1: layer 2 is vertical. Bit 7 is also set by the layer 3 setup.
Values: 0 = horizontal level.

005D.name: Screens in level
desc: Number of screens (pages) in the level, from the level header: (byte 1 & $1F) + 1.
Collision and tile lookups compare a position's screen number to it and treat anything beyond as no tile.
Mode 7 boss setup sets it to $FF so the whole range is valid.

005E.name: Horizontal screen count
desc: Number of screens in a horizontal level, as parsed from the level header; Mario's scroll limit uses it
(the camera is stopped at the last screen, $005E - 1). Game mode 11 sets it to $20; mode 7 boss setup clears it.

005F.name: Vertical screen count
desc: Number of screens in a vertical level (last screen), from the level header. 'Scroll screen to follow Mario'
reads it to stop vertical scrolling at the end of the level. Counterpart of $005E.

0064.name: Sprite priority bits
desc: OAM priority/property bits ORed into the tiles a sprite or effect draws, so Mario and sprites appear in
front of or behind the layers. Many routines set it to $10 to draw behind the layers (sprites emerging from
a block, vines growing, Piranha Plants, Yoshi in a pipe, Monty Mole popping up) and restore it afterwards.
Values: $10 = draw behind layer 1; other values = normal.

0065.name: Level data pointer (low word)
desc: General 24-bit pointer, $0065-$0067, used as a long pointer into level data. 'Load level' points it at the
layer 1 object data (and the header bytes) and the object loader reads 3 bytes at a time through it.
Layer 2 data uses $0068-$006A. 'Generate Map16 tile' loads it from the block pointer table, and the credits
code reuses it as a VRAM address ($5840) for the text rows.
Values: low 16 bits of the address.

0066.name: Level data pointer (high byte of word)
0066.kind: byte (middle byte of the pointer at $0065)
desc: Middle byte of the 24-bit pointer at $0065 (so $0065-$0066 is the 16-bit offset, $0067 the bank).
Advanced with carry when an object routine steps through level data. In the credits it is the high byte
of the text row VRAM address.

0067.name: Level data pointer bank
desc: Bank byte of the pointer at $0065. Set to the bank of the level data, or 0 / $0C for other users
(Map16 block generation, credits layer data). In the credits text code it counts the next text row instead.

0068.name: Layer 2 data pointer (low word)
desc: Low word of the 24-bit pointer $0068-$006A to the layer 2 object or background data. 'Load level' fills it,
'Switch to layer 2 objects' then copies it (plus 5 for the header) into $0065-$0067.
The credits scene setup loads it from a table; Level load reads it as a source pointer.

0069.name: Layer 2 data pointer (middle byte)
0069.kind: byte (middle byte of the pointer at $0068)
desc: High byte of the 16-bit offset of the layer 2 data pointer at $0068. Set by 'Load level' and read when
switching to layer 2 objects, where the 5-byte layer header is skipped.

006A.name: Layer 2 data pointer bank
desc: Bank of the layer 2 data. Set to $0C for prebuilt backgrounds (all of them live in bank $0C), and for the
credits compressed data. Read when the loader switches to layer 2 objects.

006B.name: Map16 low-byte pointer
desc: Long pointer to the Map16 tile low bytes of the current screen of the level buffer (bank $7E).
Level object routines store tiles through it (STA [$6B],Y) at the position in $0057, and read it back
to merge with existing tiles. The matching high-byte (tile page) pointer is $006E.
Set up by 'Load one level object' and 'Generate Map16 tile'.

006C.name: Map16 low-byte pointer (middle)
desc: Middle byte of the Map16 low-byte pointer at $006B. Object routines add $10 to the low byte to move down one
row and carry into $006C, or increment it to go to the next screen page. Mirrored in $006F.

006D.name: Map16 low-byte pointer bank
desc: Bank of the Map16 low-byte pointer; expected to be $7E. Written when a level object address is found, by
Layer 2 builders and by Generate Map16 tile ($7E), and by the credits background loader.

006E.name: Map16 high-byte pointer
desc: Long pointer to the Map16 high-byte (tile page) buffer for the current screen, bank $7F. Parallel to the
low-byte pointer at $006B; object routines mirror their pointer into it, and a high byte of 1 selects tile
page $1xx. 'Generate Map16 tile' also reads page tables with it.

006F.name: Map16 high-byte pointer (middle)
desc: Middle byte of the pointer at $006E. Always updated together with $006C when an object routine moves down a
row or to the next page. Only written, never read directly.

0070.name: Map16 high-byte pointer bank
desc: Bank of the Map16 high-byte pointer; expected to be $7F (the credits code sets $7E). Set when the object
address is found; also cleared by one level-start loop that indexes by X.

0071.name: Mario animation state
desc: Selects what Mario is doing instead of normal control: each value dispatches a special per-frame routine
(power-ups, pipes, hurt, death, door entry, scripted walks). 0 = normal handling. Written by whatever
starts the event, and cleared back to 0 when it ends.
Values: 0 normal, 1 shrinking (power down), 2 growing (mushroom), 3 cape power up, 5 horizontal pipe,
6 vertical pipe, 8 Yoshi wings exit, 9 dying, $0A scripted walk (level end), $0C castle entrance / cutscene,
$0D entering a door.

0072.name: Mario in-air state
desc: Nonzero while Mario is off the ground, 0 when he is standing. The value is the phase: swimming and jump code
set $0B while he rises and $24 while he falls. Climbing a net or vine clears it.
Read by pose selection, scrolling, water splashes, Yoshi and many sprite routines.
Values: 0 = on the ground, $0B = rising, $24 = falling.

0073.name: Mario ducking flag
desc: Nonzero while Mario is ducking. Reset to 0 every frame he is on the ground, swimming or doing cape flight,
then set when Down is held. Read by collision (hitbox), Yoshi checks and the bubble/smoke spawn routines.
Values: 0 = not ducking.

0074.name: Mario climbing flag
desc: Nonzero while Mario is climbing a net or vine. Set by copying $008B when he grabs the climbable tile,
cleared by block collision. Read by the scrolling and the carried-sprite pose code.

0075.name: Mario swimming flag
desc: Set to 1 by level collision when Mario is in water, so the physics code uses swimming speeds.
Read by the climbing tables, cape update and the screen scroll routine.
Values: 0 = not in water, 1 = swimming.

0076.name: Mario facing direction
desc: Which way Mario faces. Set when he turns on the ground, by cutscenes and by Yoshi code; read for his
acceleration, drawing and fireball direction. Used as a table index (X = facing).
Values: 0 = left, 1 = right.

0077.name: Mario blocked status
desc: Which sides of Mario are against solid tiles or the screen edge, rebuilt each frame by block collision
(set with TSB) and by sprites that carry him (platforms, rafts). Read by walking, pose and platform code.
Bits: Bit 0: blocked right. Bit 1: blocked left. Bit 2: blocked below (on ground). Bit 3: blocked above.
Bit 7: touching the left/right screen edge.

0078.name: Mario tile hide mask
desc: Mask applied to Mario's drawn tiles. 0 draws everything. Pipe and power-up animations set it to $7F (or a
computed value) to hide Mario, and the OAM drawing sets individual bits when it builds his tiles.
Platform and chain code store $FF in it, probably to cancel a remaining jump/bonk state (unclear).

007A.name: Mario X speed fraction
007A.kind: byte (sub-pixel part of the X speed)
desc: Fractional part of Mario's horizontal speed; with $007B it forms the 16-bit speed used by 'Mario X speed
on ground' (acceleration is added to the 16-bit value). Cleared to 0 when climbing.

007B.name: Mario X speed
desc: Mario's horizontal speed, signed (negative = left). Written by walking physics, collision (stop at walls),
pipes, scripted animations, springboards and bosses; added to his X position each frame.
Also set to the scroll speed when he is carried along with the screen, and by Yoshi kick-off ($10/-$10).

007D.name: Mario Y speed
desc: Mario's vertical speed, signed (negative = up). Set to jump and bounce values (e.g. $B0/$80 springboard,
$D0 balloon bounce, $90 at level start), zeroed on landing, in water entry and climbing, and pressed to
$10 while standing on a sprite. Gravity is added each frame in the Mario Y speed routine.

007E.name: Mario X on screen
desc: Mario's X position relative to the screen (his X position minus the layer 1 scroll), computed in the Mario
drawing routine. Sprites and screen-collision code compare against it (e.g. Peach, Wiggler, Layer 3 smash).
The high byte-like flag is $007F.

007F.name: Mario off-screen flag (horizontal)
desc: High byte of Mario's X on-screen position ($007E is the low byte); nonzero when he is off the screen
horizontally. ORed with $0081 by the bubble/smoke spawners, cape and misc sprite handlers to refuse
spawning effects when Mario is off screen. Read only (written by the Mario OAM drawing code).

0080.name: Mario Y on screen
desc: Mario's Y position relative to the screen, computed in the Mario drawing routine. Read by sprite contact
checks (standing on a sprite, Wiggler, Layer 3 smash, bonus block) and by the Mode 7 boss platform code.
Partner of $007E; the high byte is $0081.

0081.name: Mario off-screen flag (vertical)
desc: High byte of Mario's Y on-screen position ($0080 is the low byte); nonzero when he is vertically off screen.
Tested together with $007F before spawning bubbles and smoke, giving Mario a cape, and similar effects.
Mostly read; the disassembly shows data-table false hits for this address in sprite pointer tables.

0082.name: Slope shape table pointer
desc: Long pointer to the Map16 slope-shape table. The Map16 pointer setup stores $E55E in it (bank in $0084 is 0,
so it points at $00:E55E). The Mario block collision reads [$82],Y to get the slope shape of a tile.

0084.name: Slope shape table pointer bank
desc: Bank byte of the pointer at $0082. Set to 0 by the Map16 pointer setup. The 26 'reads' in bank $01 are
misdecoded pointer table data, not real accesses.

0085.name: Water level flag
desc: Nonzero when the current level is a water level. Set once at level start; read by the Mario collision
(which turns on swimming), the physics code (BIT tests it) and sprites that behave differently in water.
Most of the 104 listed uses are misdecoded pointer-table data, not real reads.
Values: 0 = not water, 1 = water level.
